label: verify-bm-diffusion-kinetics

claims.claim: Equilibration scales as h^2/D; one-face t50=0.197, t90=0.848, t99=1.78 h^2/D (both faces: divide by 4); optimal bilayer curvature reaches 99% at 1.65 h_a^2/D regardless of modulus ratio.
claims.note: My own Crank series gives 0.04918/0.2120/0.4453, times 4 gives 0.1967/0.848/1.781; the copied script reproduces the 1.652 curvature t99 and 1.5 ceiling, though the laminate model itself is the agent's.

claims.claim: Measured water diffusivities span four decades: polyamide/TPU/filaments 1.4e-13 to 5e-12; methacrylate resins 1.5e-12 to 1.1e-11; hydrogels and PEG-acrylates 4e-11 to 2e-10; PDMS and porous media 6e-10 to 1e-9.
claims.source_says: TPU: 'Diffusion coefficients ranged from 1.40 × 10−13 to 3.40 × 10−12 m2 s−1'. Resins: 'Bis-GMA 11.01 × 10⁻⁸ cm² s⁻¹ ... TEGDMA 1.52 × 10⁻⁸'. Hydrogel: '8.8 × 10−11 to 1.7 × 10−10 m2/s'. PDMS: 'Dwp ≃ 6–8 × 10-10 m2 s-1'.
claims.note: The first three ranges check out, but the 4e-11 hydrogel end is the agent's own inversion, the PDMS value is quoted second-hand, and the porous-media 1e-9 is a model estimate ('For molecular pores, D ~ 10-9'), not a measurement.

claims.claim: Formlabs 1 day/1 week mass data imply D about 3e-12 m2/s for Grey V5 (M_inf ~3.7%, assumed 3.2 mm) and >= 6e-12 for Flexible 80A V2 (assumed 2 mm); the '<1% in 24 h' cube numbers are far from equilibrium (10 mm cube at D=1e-12 reaches ~19% of plateau).
claims.source_says: Grey V5 TDS, DI Water row, MASS column: 101.38% (1 day), 103.23% (1 week). Flexible 80A V2: Deionized Water 1 day -26 +8% +3% 94% 89%; 1 week -27 +9% +7% 101% 88%.
claims.note: I confirmed both TDS values by PDF word coordinates (text extraction scrambles rows) and reproduced D=3.30e-12, 9.32e-12 and the cube figure (18.6% by my own calculation), but the D values rest entirely on the agent's assumed specimen thicknesses, which the TDS does not state.

claims.claim: A demonstration finishing in hours needs D >= 1e-11 with a 0.2-0.8 mm active layer; stock rigid resins (D~1e-12) at 0.2-0.4 mm give 9-38 h; 0.8 mm or more, or dense nylon/TPU, take days to weeks.
claims.note: The arithmetic reproduces from 0.848 h^2/D; the verdict inherits the D assumptions from the other claims and is a model calculation, not a measurement.

overall: Three of four key claims reproduce: the Crank constants, the script outputs, and both Formlabs TDS mass tables (checked by PDF word position). The diffusivity-range claim is only partly supported, because some ends of the ranges are derived or second-hand rather than measured. The Formlabs and demonstration claims depend on assumed specimen thicknesses, which the TDS sheets do not state.
